question: Y038 LFU frequency advantage was adverse at slow home drift1. Does updating cached motif priority only when a previously stored placement is actually legal at reentry reduce the value of stale frequency counts while maintaining four-slot capacity?
hypothesis: When legal placement persistence is imperfect, legal-hit frequency may retain truly reusable motifs better than any-hit LFU; it may also forget frequently returning motifs in temporary displacement.
world: Exact frozen Y038 keyed 16-motif hot/cold schedule and paired-collision geometry with drift D=1 only, fixed before run. Seven active, four inactive cached slots, 16 episodes; new development seeds120..123, heldout124..127. The source already pins the parameter family; new trial does NOT rerun consumed Y038 results.
arms: LRU four-slot baseline with identical two-bit counter metadata
any-hit LFU updates capped counter on every observed cached-key reentry

LEGAL-HIT LFU increments its capped two-bit reentry count only when cached cell is currently within legal radius2 neighborhood; illegal reentry resets count to1. Eviction otherwise selects lowest count, ties oldest/key
controls: Same four inactive cache slots plus seven active assignments and counter bits in every arm. No future schedule, hot-key status, experiment labels or oracle calls exposed to policy. Independent exhaustive Hall oracle is evaluator-only. Real cache evictions required in every arm and heldout seed.
primary: Per-seed returning hot-motif churn, total returning churn, legal cached preferences, actual evictions, writes/search calls and unique geometry SHA signatures. LEGAL_HIT_LEARNING_BENEFIT if legal-hit LFU hot churn lower aggregate than any-hit LFU and all churn no worse and hot churn not worse in >=3/4 seeds, with 7 matching and genuine evictions. MIXED if hot better but all worse; NEGATIVE otherwise; INVALID for Hall/capacity/signature; CAUSAL_TEST_UNEXERCISED if eviction absent.
claim_limit: Finite synthetic online legality-gated frequency memory, not natural intelligence or biological consolidation.
